concept: ContextMenu wraps one object on the page and opens Menu's plastic panel of actions at the point the person pressed, by right-click, long-press or the Context Menu key; while it is open the object sinks into a well so the panel says which object it is for.

default_to_avoid.pattern: context menu that replaces the browser menu and is the only way to reach an action
default_to_avoid.why_not: Right-click and long-press are hidden gestures that touch, switch and screen reader users may never find, so every action must also be on a visible key such as Menu.

default_to_avoid.pattern: context menu card with a blue highlighted row and a tinted backdrop over the whole page
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tinted bar tells position by colour alone and a page-wide scrim hides the object the menu is about, against P1 where only the one primary control is coloured.

references.source: Braun TG 60 tape recorder (Dieter Rams, 1965): a lid that opens over the part you point at and prints its functions in plain words, in the same panel as the other lids
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: menu pattern and the Context Menu key / Shift+F10 convention (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu/)
WCAG 2.2 · 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures and 2.1.1 Keyboard: an action must not depend on a path-based or hidden gesture alone (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures.html)

derivation.form: The panel is Menu's own panel, surface.solid with elevation.float and corner.inner on layer.overlay, so a person learns one popup; the object it belongs to sinks into elevation.well instead of getting a second shadow.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Rows are primary ink, the open object is told by a recess and a destructive row by the critical square, and nothing in the area or the panel is orange.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Each row is at least control.md tall as in Menu, and the panel is kept on the screen so a finger can always reach every row.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: The Context Menu key and Shift+F10 open the panel on the first action, arrows, Home, End and letters move, Escape closes and returns focus to where it was, and a 500ms touch press does the same as a right-click.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The panel rises in and sinks out on Menu's release and exit motion through presence, and the object's well fades on motion.hover; nothing moves while it sits open.

options.name: panel corner at the pointer with a small ink index dot marking the point
panel corner at the pointer and the pressed object sinks into a well while the panel is open
flat bordered legend panel on the page colour joined to the point by a printed hairline

variants.reason: B says which object the menu is for by depth alone, so it needs no extra mark and works on any size of object; A adds a dot that is easily hidden under a finger, and C breaks the one-popup rule by drawing a second panel material and its line crosses the content it names (P8 lines never cross a label).

root.why: The root is the object the menu belongs to; it listens for the right-click, the long-press and the Context Menu key, and it sinks into a well while the panel is open.

data-open.why: While the panel is open the object it belongs to is a recess in elevation.well, so depth tells which object the actions are for and the cue survives a greyscale screen.

focus-visible.why: An object that takes focus so the Context Menu key can reach it shows the same dark ring as every part.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well is removed by the system, so the open object keeps a real Highlight outline as its cue.

background-color.why: The object sinks into its well on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the change reads as a part settling and not a flash.

box-shadow.why: The object sinks into its well on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the change reads as a part settling and not a flash.
